beats.say: What does TSMC do? It makes chips that other companies design. And it keeps fifty one dollars of every hundred it sells. How does a factory keep half? Picture a castle, with deep water all around it.

cues: It makes chips that other companies design.
And it keeps $51 of every $100 it sells.
How does a factory keep half?

beats.say: TSMC is Priya, for chips. Companies like Apple and Nvidia design chips. TSMC builds them. From July to September, that brought in forty six point seven billion dollars.
beats.cap: TSMC is Priya, for chips. Companies like Apple and Nvidia design chips. TSMC builds them. From July to September 2026, that brought in $46.7 billion.
cues: Companies like Apple and Nvidia design chips.
From July to September 2026, that brought in $46.7 billion.

beats.say: By the end, you will run our three question moat test on TSMC. First: who pays it?
beats.cap: By the end, you will run our 3-question moat test on TSMC. First: who pays it?
cues: By the end, you will run our 3-question moat test on TSMC.

beats.say: Who pays TSMC? Mostly companies that make chips for A I and data centres. Of every hundred dollars, about sixty eight came from them. Smartphones paid about twenty one. Everything else, about eleven.
beats.cap: Who pays TSMC? Mostly companies that make chips for AI and data centres. Of every $100, about $68 came from them. Smartphones paid about $21. Everything else, about $11.
cues: Mostly companies that make chips for AI and data centres.
Of every $100, about $68 came from them.

beats.say: A year ago, A I chip makers paid about fifty seven of every hundred. Now, sixty eight. So the castle now stands on A I. Why does that help TSMC keep more?
beats.cap: A year ago, AI chip makers paid about $57 of every $100. Now, $68. So the castle now stands on AI. Why does that help TSMC keep more?
cues: A year ago, AI chip makers paid about $57 of every $100.
So the castle now stands on AI.
Why does that help TSMC keep more?

beats.say: How much does TSMC keep? Fifty one dollars of every hundred. Not ten. Not twenty five. A year ago, it kept about forty six.
beats.cap: How much does TSMC keep? $51 of every $100. Not $10. Not $25. A year ago, it kept about $46 (our arithmetic).

scene.heading: TSMC SELLS $100. WHAT DOES IT KEEP?

cues: A year ago, it kept about $46 (our arithmetic).

beats.say: Follow one hundred dollars. Making the chips takes about thirty three. Running the company takes about eight. Tax takes about eight more. Fifty one is left.
beats.cap: Follow $100. Making the chips takes about $33. Running the company takes about $8. Tax takes about $8 more. $51 is left (our arithmetic; tax is after interest income).

beats.say: And the share it keeps is growing. In a year, sales grew by half. Profit grew by two thirds.
beats.cap: And the share it keeps is growing. In a year, sales grew by half (+50.9%). Profit grew by two thirds (+68.7%, in Taiwan dollars).
cues: And the share it keeps is growing.
In a year, sales grew by half (+50.9%).
Profit grew by two thirds (+68.7%, in Taiwan dollars).

beats.say: Why can't rivals copy TSMC? Because very few can make the newest chips. Chip makers name each new step by size. Smaller is newer, and harder to make.
beats.cap: Why can't rivals copy TSMC? Because very few can make the newest chips. Chip makers name each new step by size, in nanometres. Smaller is newer, and harder to make.
cues: Because very few can make the newest chips.
Chip makers name each new step by size, in nanometres.
Smaller is newer, and harder to make.

beats.say: Of every hundred dollars of chips TSMC sold, thirty three were the three nanometre size. Twenty eight were five. Ten were seven. The newest, two, is already eight. Older sizes: twenty one.
beats.cap: Of every $100 of chips TSMC sold, $33 were the 3-nanometre size. $28 were 5. $10 were 7. The newest, 2, is already $8. Older sizes: $21.
cues: Of every $100 of chips TSMC sold, $33 were the 3-nanometre size.

beats.say: Add up the newest four. Seventy nine of every hundred dollars. That is the water around the castle. A new chip factory costs billions of dollars. And it takes years to run one well.
beats.cap: Add up the newest four: $79 of every $100. That is the water around the castle. A new chip factory costs billions of dollars. And it takes years to run one well.
cues: That is the water around the castle.
A new chip factory costs billions of dollars.
And it takes years to run one well.

beats.say: Why did TSMC's margin slip? Because costs grew faster than sales, against April to June. Sales grew seventeen point six percent. Profit grew only eight.
beats.cap: Why did TSMC's margin slip? Because costs grew faster than sales, against April to June. Sales grew 17.6%. Profit grew only 8.0%.
cues: Because costs grew faster than sales, against April to June.

beats.say: The gross margin is what is left after making the chips. It fell from about sixty seven point seven percent to sixty six point four. Small, on a very big base.
beats.cap: The gross margin is what is left after making the chips. It fell from about 67.7% to 66.4%. Small, on a very big base.

beats.say: What does TSMC expect next? About the same margins, or a little lower. For October to December, its gross margin guide is sixty five to sixty seven percent. Last quarter: sixty six point four.

beats.say: Does TSMC pass our moat test? Ask our three questions. One: can a rival with money and time copy it? Two: must it be rebuilt again and again? Three: does it walk out with one person?

beats.say: Copy it? Very hard, on our reading. Rebuild it? Yes. Every new size costs billions again. One person? No. So: a wide moat, that must be dug again every few years.

beats.say: Quick recap. What does TSMC do? Makes chips others design. Who pays? Mostly A I chip makers. What does it keep? Fifty one of every hundred. Why can't rivals copy it? The newest chips are hard to make. The slip? Costs grew faster. Next? About the same. The test? A wide moat, dug again.
